enhanced_information: Urea is a polar molecule produced in the liver as part of the urea cycle, where it is synthesized from arginine through the hydrolysis of arginine to produce urea and ornithine. It is then transported to the kidneys for elimination in urine, not the liver. Urea is not degraded to ammonium in the urea cycle; instead, it is excreted as urea. It is soluble in water and does not easily form crystals. Structurally, urea contains two amine groups and one carbonyl group, not two ketone groups. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, confirm the association of urea with liver processes and its synthesis from arginine, aligning with the consensus that urea is part of the metabolic processes involving the liver and arginine.
